Target n=10 (round_robin_arbiter_pb_10_pe_.ltl) is UNKNOWN with a precisely identified root cause, not a correctness defect: this family's formula is one Assume -> And(guarantees) implication (needed extending the conjunct decomposer to split an implication's consequent while retaining the full antecedent, done, families/proposals/verify_conjuncts.py), but the shared ASSUME antecedent itself -- a 10-way conjunction of independent per-client weak-fairness terms on disjoint APs -- has a genuinely exponential automaton: measured 3^n states (n=5: 243, n=6: 729), confirmed independent of host load (retried at measurably lighter campaign memory pressure, still failed; translating the antecedent alone, nothing else running, does not complete in 90s) and independent of Spot's acceptance-type translate option. This is exactly the 'eager checking is the obstacle' condition the plan names as W6's trigger (candidate-restricted product construction); not implemented this session. An earlier host-contention hypothesis recorded during this investigation is superseded by this more precise, better-evidenced finding.

families.valid_parameter_predicate: template default n=2; the added poison INVARIANTS clause is `&&[0<=i<n]( &&[i<j<n] (r[i] && X r[j] -> F(g[i] && g[j])) )`, which is a vacuously true empty conjunction for n=1 -- meaning n=1 would NOT be a valid instantiation of the intended unrealizable obstruction (it would likely be realizable, same as the base round_robin_arbiter). Valid range for this family's intended obstruction is therefore n>=2, not n>=1 as the bare template comment would suggest; not yet independently confirmed by an actual n=1 solve.

families.status: selected and justified from the actual template. Confirmed by direct code reading (not assumed from the handoff's caution alone) that Acacia's -s never exports a controller for an unreal-arm win: src/arg_parser.hh strips extra real arms when -s is given but keeps all unreal arms in the portfolio, and src/solver/solver_invoker.cc:715 asserts synth_fname and check_unreal are mutually exclusive on the main solve path. Also checked ltlsynt (Spot's own synthesis tool, already installed): --aiger prints nothing at all when the instance is UNREALIZABLE (verified directly: `ltlsynt --tlsf=.../round_robin_arbiter_unreal2.tlsf/n=2 --aiger --verify` prints only 'UNREALIZABLE' to stdout, exit 1, no AIG) -- ltlsynt is not a pinned existing exporter for this either. Traced the transformation Acacia's own UNREAL_X_FORMULA worker applies internally (solver_invoker.cc ~1090-1095 and ~421-433): swap input_aps<->output_aps, wrap every atom that was an ORIGINAL output in X(), do NOT negate the objective. Attempted a paper (not executed) differential check of the naive TLSF-level version of this recipe on a hand-picked tiny unrealizable game (G(o <-> X(i)) under Mealy, whose only fair environment strategy is the trivial, obviously-causal i(t+1):=not(o(t))) and found the naive swap+shift, read back literally, produces the swapped game's trivial i:=o combinational strategy -- which, mapped back to the original game's round order without further reinterpretation, would let the environment's move at t+1 depend on the system's move at the SAME t+1, i.e. use information not yet available: exactly the kind of unsound, clairvoyant witness plan section 7.1 forbids ('not allowed to... use future information'). This means the TLSF-level reconstruction needs a circuit-level clock realignment beyond the formula-level swap+shift that this session could not derive with confidence. The safer next step identified instead: extend Acacia itself (remove the solver_invoker.cc:715 assert and route synth_fname through for the unreal-formula worker, which is already dualization-aware internally per run_one_ltl::synthesis()) rather than reconstruct the dualization externally -- this needs a C++ change and rebuild, appropriately deferred until the campaign reaches a quiet window. Deferred deliberately, not abandoned, and not attempted in an unsafe way: two negative results (Acacia's -s, ltlsynt's --aiger) and one caught near-miss are real, useful findings on their own.
